answer: Escrowed history weighting: each agent identity carries a public record of solved tasks whose weight grows with age, and rewards route only through records older than a fixed window. A clone starts at zero weight, so it must fund a full window of genuine work before earning anything, paying compute and delay per identity while the original keeps its accumulated pearl. Identity resets also forfeit the record, so copying the quill of past work gains nothing without the nebula of elapsed time the ledger demands.
